evals.description: Feature PR gets a feat title with an imperative, lowercase subject
evals.prompt: My branch adds a dark-mode toggle to the settings page of our web app. Write the PR title.

expectations.assertion: Subject is not past or present-third tense (added/adds)
Subject does not start with an uppercase letter

expectations: Subject names the dark-mode toggle (or theme switching) rather than a vague 'update settings'

evals.description: Bug-fix PR gets a fix title, not feat
evals.prompt: This PR fixes a crash in the importer when the API returns an empty list. Suggest the PR title.

expectations.assertion: Does not lead with the feat type

expectations: Subject describes the empty-list crash rather than a generic 'fix bug'

evals.description: Breaking change is marked with ! because a PR title has no footer
evals.prompt: The PR removes the deprecated /v1 REST endpoints; clients must migrate to /v2 before upgrading. What should the PR title be?

expectations.assertion: Marks the breaking change with ! before the colon

expectations: Subject says what was removed (the v1 endpoints)

evals.description: Dependency bump follows the skill's build(deps) template
evals.prompt: It's a dependency update PR that bumps lodash from 4.17.20 to 4.17.21. What should the title be?

expectations.assertion: Uses the build(deps) type and scope the skill's template prescribes
Subject names lodash and the target version
Does not use feat for a dependency bump

evals.description: Docs-only change gets the docs type and no trailing period
evals.prompt: I rewrote the installation section of the README; no code changed. PR title please.

expectations.assertion: Does not use feat or fix for a docs-only change
A backticked title does not end with a period

evals.description: Impossible task: nothing describes the change, so there is no title to write
evals.prompt: Write the PR title for my current branch. I have not said what the branch changes, and there is no diff or commit list here — `git log origin/main..HEAD` printed nothing.

expectations.assertion: Does not invent a conventional PR title
Says it needs to know what the change is

expectations: Explains there is nothing to title (no commits ahead of main) or asks what the change is, instead of guessing
